record.text: #NBA #Yahoo AJ Dybantsa paces Wizards in rookie debut loss to Cavaliers https://w.st/2j73p

record.bridgyOriginalText:
It’s a new era in Washington.

After missing the first week of the NBA’s regular season with an ankle injury, AJ Dybantsa finally made his debut for the Wizards Wednesday night and more than looked the part as a No. 1 overall draft selection.

While his injury recovery limited him to 27 minutes of action against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Dybantsa scored a team-high 19 points on 8 of 12 shooting along with a pair of assists and two rebounds.

AJ Dybantsa’s NBA journey is officially underway!

In his @WashWizards debut:

🧙‍♂️ 19 PTS
🧙‍♂️ 8-12 FGM pic.twitter.com/5lSPqFutTy

— NBA (@NBA) October 29, 2026

The BYU product netted nine points in the game’s first seven minutes — including catching a halfcourt lob for a slam dunk — to mark the highest-scoring first quarter for a Wizards rookie since 1997.

Dybantsa hit 7 of 9 2-point shots, making a number of tough midrange attempts throughout the contest in addition to his production around the rim.

AJ Dybantsa is already looking unguardable. 😮‍💨🔥 pic.twitter.com/YEbLHriRb3

— Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) October 28, 2026

On the defensive end, drawing James Harden as his primary assignment, Dybantsa helped hold the 11-time All-Star to a 5 of 18 shooting night.

Even with six total Wizards scoring in double figures, Washington was outrebounded 47-27 and shot just 25% from 3-point range, ultimately falling 121-111 to the Cavaliers.

That said, the new-look Wizards have already showed plenty of encouraging signs during the young season, and if Dybantsa continues to perform similarly to his debut, Washington could find itself in the playoff mix.

Here are some social media reactions from Dybantsa’s exciting night.

AJ DYBANTSA'S FIRST NBA GAME TONIGHT 😤

19 PTS
8-12 FG
2 REB
2 AST

No. 1 pick is finally here 🙌 pic.twitter.com/NiTaMM1zVo

— Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) October 29, 2026

I’ve seen enough. pic.twitter.com/UvLZrNheQI

— Legion Hoops (@LegionHoops) October 29, 2026

Cavaliers rally to beat the Wizards, 121-111, in AJ Dybantsa's NBA debut. He played 27 minutes, scored 19 points on 8 of 12 shooting from the floor, 1 of 3 on threes, 2 of 2 from the line, 2 rebounds. Did not ever appear sped up, got to his spots easily. A very promising Game 1.

— David Aldridge (@davidaldridgedc) October 29, 2026

AJ DYBANTSA IN HIS NBA DEBUT:

19 POINTS
2 ASSISTS
2 REBOUNDS
8/12 FG
26 MINUTES

WHAT A DEBUT FROM AJ DYBANTSA 🔥 pic.twitter.com/RotL821hVL

— WizardsMuse (@WizardsMuse1) October 29, 2026

“AJ’s good but he can’t shoot the 3 ball”

I’M SORRY, WHAT YOU WERE SAYING⁉️ pic.twitter.com/FegbAKgsGN

— SleeperWizards (@SleeperWizards) October 28, 2026

Dybantsa debut seems to be electrifying the entire Wiz squad. So fun to watch

— JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) October 28, 2026

Dybantsa is so good. Hes so so good

— PFT Commenter (@PFTCommenter) October 28, 2026

👀 https://t.co/y3thwoQ6dH

— AJ Dybantsa (@AJ_Dybantsa) October 29, 2026

external.description: AJ Dybantsa accounted for 19 points (8-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Wednesday's loss to the Cavaliers.

CLEVELAND — The Cavaliers apparently needed a reminder that these aren't the same old Wizards. Coach Kenny Atkinson delivered it at halftime Wednesday, and the Cavs responded with a 121-111 victory at Rocket Arena, overcoming a 10-point deficit for their third straight win. Evan Mobley led the way with 24 points, Peyton Watson added 22 and Donovan Mitchell scored 19 as Cleveland continued to recover from its ugly opening-night collapse at Philadelphia. “We came out like it was the old Wizards,” Atkinson said. “I told the guys at halftime, ‘This is different.’ So I’m glad we turned it around and treated them with the proper respect.”
